items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: Find the word with a capital letter.
Find the word with a full stop.
Start with the capital letter.
items.explanation: I like red apples. It starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

items.prompt: Look at the picture. Write one sentence about the cat.
hints: Say your sentence out loud first.
Count the words on your fingers.
You can start with: The cat.
items.explanation: A good sentence starts with a capital letter, has finger spaces and ends with a full stop.
items.model: The cat is sitting on the mat.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: The first word has a capital letter.
The last word has a full stop.
Read your sentence. Does it make sense?
items.explanation: My dog can run fast. It starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

items.prompt: Which one is a whole sentence?
hints: A sentence tells a whole idea.
It needs who or what, and what they do.
Look for a capital letter and a full stop too.
items.explanation: The cat sleeps on the bed tells us who and what they do. It is a whole sentence.

options.why: This does not tell us who or what.

options.text: The cat sleeps on the bed.

options.why: This does not say what the cat does.

hints: Finger spaces go between words.
Look for squashed words.
Check each gap between the words.
items.explanation: I can see a bird. has a space between every word.

options.why: Can and see need a space between them.

items.prompt: Write a sentence about your favourite food.
hints: You can start with: My favourite food is.
Add a describing word, like sweet or crunchy.
items.explanation: Name the food and say something about it. Remember the capital letter and the full stop.

criteria.label: Says how it tastes or why you like it

planning: What food do you like best?
items.model: My favourite food is fried rice. It is yummy.

items.prompt: Which word makes the best sentence? 'I write with a ___.'
hints: Read the sentence with each word.
Think about what you hold to write.
Which one would your teacher give you?
items.explanation: We write with a pencil, so I write with a pencil makes sense.

options.why: You do not write with a banana.
You do not write with a bed.

items.prompt: Write two sentences about the weather today.
hints: Look out of the window first.
Your first sentence can start with: It is.
items.explanation: Two sentences means two capital letters and two full stops.

criteria.label: Uses a weather word, like sunny or rainy

planning: Is it sunny, rainy, windy or cloudy?
items.model: It is rainy today. I can see big grey clouds.

hints: Check the first letter.
Check the end.
Find the one with a capital letter and a full stop.
items.explanation: The sun is hot. starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

options.why: It needs a capital letter and a full stop.
It needs a full stop at the end.
The first word needs a capital letter.

items.prompt: Write two or three sentences about someone in your family.
hints: Start with who the person is.
Then say what they like to do.
items.explanation: Tell the reader who the person is and something they do. Names and I always have a capital letter.

criteria.label: Capital letters for names and for I

planning: What do they like to do?
items.model: My grandma is kind. She makes me rice cakes. I help her in the garden.

items.prompt: Look at the pictures. Write a sentence for each one.

figure.alt: Three pictures joined by arrows: a seed, a small seedling, then a flower.

hints: Look at the first picture. What is it?
Use words like first, next and then.
items.explanation: Write one sentence for each picture, in the same order as the pictures.

criteria.label: Words in an order that makes sense

items.model: I plant a seed. It grows into a small plant. Now it has a flower.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: The word with a capital letter starts the sentence.
The word with a comma comes second.
Read it aloud to check it makes sense.
items.explanation: After school, we play in the park.

items.prompt: Write three sentences about an animal you like. Use a describing word.
hints: Start with: I like.
Use a describing word for its size, colour or fur.
items.explanation: Say which animal you like, what it looks like and what it can do.

criteria.label: Uses a describing word, like big or soft

items.model: I like elephants. An elephant is big and grey. It has a long trunk.

items.prompt: Write a short story about a lost toy. Say what happens first, next and at the end.
hints: Start with what the toy is.
Use first, next and then for the places you look.
End with how you feel.
items.explanation: A story needs a beginning, a middle and an end. Time words like first, next and then show the order.

criteria.label: Has a beginning, a middle and an end

planning: How do you feel at the end?
items.model: Yesterday I lost my teddy. First, I looked under my bed. Next, I looked in the garden. Then I found him in the toy box! I was so happy.
